lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The house has gone quiet in Toronto, and not in the good way. The Maple Leafs finished their six-game homestand winless after falling 1-0 to Edmonton on Nov. 14, a fourth straight defeat that leaves them 8-12, 13th in the Eastern Conference, with 18 points and a six-game losing streak. The offense has vanished at the worst possible time: Toronto has been shut out twice in its last four games, and the latest loss turned John Chayka's choices into a public debate - fire the coach, make a trade, or stand pat and accept the slide. There is no easy answer, but the blue line plainly needs attention. Now comes a road test with Chicago. Tuesday's 7:30 p.m. visit to the Blackhawks is less about a cure than proof of life - and whether this skid has finally reached its bottom.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: Toronto's winter has begun with the sound of a broom clearing clutter from the organization. The season is over, and the Blue Jays' final points total was -2.0 - context, not a headline - but the next roster cannot be built on wishful thinking. Toronto released 11 minor-leaguers over the past several days, a cold reminder that organizational depth needs more than familiar names. Anthony Santander, meanwhile, has become the club's designated villain, which may say as much about the fan base's frustration as the player himself. The smarter conversation is offense: internal improvement must accompany outside ambition, with Seiya Suzuki and Jazz Chisholm Jr. among the reported targets. A minor-league deal for Yeuris Jiménez adds pitching depth, but hardly changes the equation. Watch whether Toronto turns its offensive blueprint into a meaningful acquisition before camp opens March 25 at Yankee Stadium.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The Raptors keep finding new ways to lose games they had by the throat. Sunday's 112-108 overtime defeat to the Knicks spoiled Scottie Barnes' return after a four-game absence with a left groin strain, despite his 30-point, nine-rebound performance and a late three-pointer that forced overtime. That is the encouraging part. The indictment is sharper: Toronto has now lost four straight, seven of nine, and sits 5-8, fourth in the Atlantic Division, six games behind. Barnes looked like the team's engine again; Kawhi Leonard remains sidelined with a swollen left knee, and Toronto has gone 5-8 without him. The Raptors led by 13 in the fourth quarter Sunday and still watched Jalen Brunson's dagger three settle the matter. The Knicks return Tuesday at 7:30 p.m. ET, giving Toronto an immediate chance to stop the skid - or prove this collapse is becoming its identity.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The Commanders didn't win cleanly Thursday night; they won hard, late and just in time. Washington's 24-21 victory over the Giants - secured by Stefon Diggs' last-minute touchdown after Jayden Daniels threw two fourth-quarter interceptions - kept a fraying season from snapping. The defense got burned, stayed aggressive and, in the final two minutes, found the nerve to save the night. Luke McCaffrey's savvy use of the out-of-bounds rule was the sort of small, sharp detail that separates survival from regret. At 3-5-1, Washington sits second in the NFC East, two games back, with a one-game winning streak and no room for self-congratulation. Athan Kaliakmanis was inactive Thursday but remained the emergency quarterback; the larger concern is keeping Daniels upright and steadier. Next comes Cincinnati on Monday night, Nov. 23 at 8:15 p.m. ET - a test of whether this was a revival or merely a reprieve.

article.title: Knicks Beat Raptors in Overtime
paragraphs: The Raptors lost 112-108 to the Knicks in overtime Sunday, despite Scottie Barnes scoring 30 points in his return. Mouhamadou Gueye Murray-Boyles added 13 rebounds and Immanuel Quickley had six assists. Toronto, now 5-8, hosts New York again Tuesday at 7:30 p.m.

The Leafs head to Chicago Tuesday at 7:30 p.m. on TSN after losing to Edmonton and going winless through their six-game homestand. Toronto is 8-12 and 13th in the Eastern Conference. The Blue Jays are looking toward 2027, with Anthony Santander drawing attention and internal offensive improvement on the agenda; their next game is March 25 at Yankee Stadium, where the regular season opens at 1:35 p.m.

The Commanders, 3-5-1 and second in the NFC East, host Cincinnati next Monday at 8:15 p.m. on ESPN. Washington's recent conversation includes Luke McCaffrey's use of an out-of-bounds rule and backup quarterback Sam Hartman being announced as "The Bachelor."
